source: Samsung Washing Machine User Manual WA21A8376G*/WA19A8376G* (DC68-04154A-01_IB_A2_WA8800A_EN_TH_MY_231005)
content: Does not start. Door not closed; water taps closed; Hold to Start not pressed; Child Lock activated; door opened during the spinning cycle; fuse blown or circuit breaker tripped. Clicking noises before filling and a Standby or soaking cycle are normal. 1. Make sure the door is closed. 2. Make sure the water taps are open. 3. Make sure to press or tap Hold to Start to start the washing machine. 4. Make sure Child Lock is not activated. 5. Before the washing machine starts to fill, it will make a series of clicking noises to check the door lock and does a quick drain. 6. Was the door opened during the spinning cycle? Close the door, and press or tap Hold to Start to resume. 7. The machine enters Standby or is in a soaking cycle. Please wait. 8. Check the fuse or reset the circuit breaker.

metadata.symptom: Does not start.

metadata.solution:
1. Make sure the door is closed.
2. Make sure the water taps are open.
3. Make sure to press or tap Hold to Start to start the washing machine.
4. Make sure Child Lock is not activated.
5. Before the washing machine starts to fill, it will make a series of clicking noises to check the door lock and does a quick drain.
6. Was the door opened during the spinning cycle? Close the door, and press or tap Hold to Start to resume.
7. The machine enters Standby or is in a soaking cycle. Please wait.
8. Check the fuse or reset the circuit breaker.

source: Samsung Washing Machine User Manual WA21A8376G*/WA19A8376G* (DC68-04154A-01_IB_A2_WA8800A_EN_TH_MY_231005)
content: Water is not supplied. Hold to Start not pressed after selecting the water supply; water taps closed; filter net at the water supply hose connector clogged; water supply cut off; water supply hoses kinked; low water pressure. 1. Make sure you press or tap Hold to Start after selecting the water supply. 2. Make sure the water taps are open. 3. Is the filter net at the water supply hose connector clogged? Clean the filter net by brushing with a toothbrush. 4. Is the water supply cut off? If the water supply is cut off, close the tap and power off. 5. Straighten the water supply hoses. 6. Open and close the door, then press or tap Hold to Start. 7. If the water pressure is low, it takes longer to start washing. 8. If the water level is not as high as necessary or lower than expected, use the level selector to adjust the water level.

metadata.symptom: Water is not supplied.
metadata.possible_cause: Hold to Start not pressed after selecting the water supply; water taps closed; filter net at the water supply hose connector clogged; water supply cut off; water supply hoses kinked; low water pressure.
metadata.solution:
1. Make sure you press or tap Hold to Start after selecting the water supply.
2. Make sure the water taps are open.
3. Is the filter net at the water supply hose connector clogged? Clean the filter net by brushing with a toothbrush.
4. Is the water supply cut off? If the water supply is cut off, close the tap and power off.
5. Straighten the water supply hoses.
6. Open and close the door, then press or tap Hold to Start.
7. If the water pressure is low, it takes longer to start washing.
8. If the water level is not as high as necessary or lower than expected, use the level selector to adjust the water level.

content: Vibrates excessively or makes noise. Floor not level; washing machine contacting another object; unbalanced laundry; objects around the machine; coins or other objects in the machine. Humming during operation is normal. 1. Make sure the washing machine is set on a level floor. If the floor is not level, use the levelling feet to adjust the washing machine. 2. Make sure the washing machine is not contacting any other object. 3. Make sure the laundry load is balanced. 4. Make sure the laundry is spread evenly in the washing machine. Spread out the laundry evenly and start again. 5. Make sure the space around the washing machine is free of objects. 6. Humming is produced normally during operation. 7. Objects such as coins can cause noise. Remove these objects from the washing machine after washing is complete.

content: Stops. Power cord not plugged into a live outlet; fuse blown or circuit breaker tripped; door not closed or Hold to Start not pressed; inlet hose screens at the taps clogged; low voltage. A pause or soak period in the cycle and clicking noises before filling are normal. 1. Plug the power cord into a live electrical outlet. 2. Check the fuse or reset the circuit breaker. 3. Close the door, and press or tap Hold to Start to start the washing machine. For your safety, the washing machine will not spin unless the door is closed. 4. Before the washing machine starts to fill, it will make a series of clicking noises to check the door lock and does a quick drain. 5. There may be a pause or soak period in the cycle. Wait briefly and the washing machine may start. 6. Make sure the inlet hose screens at the taps are not clogged. Periodically clean the screens. 7. This problem occurs temporarily due to low voltages, and will be solved when power recovers.

metadata.symptom: Stops.
metadata.possible_cause: Power cord not plugged into a live outlet; fuse blown or circuit breaker tripped; door not closed or Hold to Start not pressed; inlet hose screens at the taps clogged; low voltage. A pause or soak period in the cycle and clicking noises before filling are normal.
metadata.solution:
1. Plug the power cord into a live electrical outlet.
2. Check the fuse or reset the circuit breaker.
3. Close the door, and press or tap Hold to Start to start the washing machine. For your safety, the washing machine will not spin unless the door is closed.
4. Before the washing machine starts to fill, it will make a series of clicking noises to check the door lock and does a quick drain.
5. There may be a pause or soak period in the cycle. Wait briefly and the washing machine may start.
6. Make sure the inlet hose screens at the taps are not clogged. Periodically clean the screens.
7. This problem occurs temporarily due to low voltages, and will be solved when power recovers.

content: The ECO TUB CLEAN alarm does not turn off. The machine is diagnosed to be cleaned. This is normal, and not a system failure. When the machine is diagnosed to be cleaned, the ECO TUB CLEAN indicator blinks for an hour. This recurs 6 consecutive times until you run the ECO TUB CLEAN cycle. This is normal, and not a system failure. To keep the tub clean, it is recommended to run the cycle once every 1-3 months.

source: Samsung Washing Machine User Manual WA21A8376G*/WA19A8376G* (DC68-04154A-01_IB_A2_WA8800A_EN_TH_MY_231005)
content: Fills with the wrong temperature water. Water taps not fully open; wrong temperature selection; hoses connected to the wrong water taps; hose filter screens clogged. Temperature changes during filling are a normal function of the automatic temperature control. 1. Fully open both water taps. 2. Make sure the temperature selection is correct. 3. Make sure the hoses are connected to the correct water taps. Flush water lines. 4. Disconnect the hoses and clean the screens. The hose filter screens may be clogged. 5. While the washing machine fills, the water temperature may change as the automatic temperature control feature checks incoming water temperature. This is normal. 6. While the washing machine fills, you may notice just hot and/or just cold water going through the dispenser when cold or warm temperatures are selected. This is a normal function of the automatic temperature control feature as the washing machine determines the water temperature.

1. Fully open both water taps.
2. Make sure the temperature selection is correct.
3. Make sure the hoses are connected to the correct water taps. Flush water lines.

content: Does not drain and/or spin. Fuse blown or circuit breaker tripped; abnormal electrical voltage; power cord not completely plugged in; drain hose not pointed downward, clogged or kinked; door not closed. 1. Check the fuse or reset the circuit breaker. 2. Make sure the electrical voltage is normal. 3. Make sure the washing machine is plugged in. 4. Make sure the drain hose is pointed downward. (Natural drain models only) 5. Make sure the drain hose is not clogged. 6. Make sure the drain hose is not kinked. 7. Straighten the drain hose. If there is a drain restriction, call for service. 8. Close the door, and press or tap Hold to Start. For your safety, the washing machine will not spin unless the door is closed.

source: Samsung Washing Machine User Manual WA21A8376G*/WA19A8376G* (DC68-04154A-01_IB_A2_WA8800A_EN_TH_MY_231005)
content: Leaks water. Hose connections loose; water supply hose rubber packing out of position; drain hose end not correctly inserted and secured; overloading; non-HE detergent causing oversudsing; water supply hose kinked; water supply too strong; leak from the water tap. 1. Make sure all hose connections are tight. 2. Make sure the water supply hose's rubber packing is in the correct position. Screw tightly again. 3. Make sure the end of the drain hose is correctly inserted and secured to the drain system. 4. Avoid overloading. 5. Use high efficiency (HE) detergent to prevent oversudsing. 6. Make sure the water supply hose is not kinked. 7. If the water supply is too strong, water may leak. Close the water tap a little. 8. Make sure water is not leaking from the water tap. If so, repair the water tap.
